about: The web build's size budget (#3622): the ONE place the numbers live. tool/web/size_budget_check.mjs compares a request trace (tool/web/first_load_trace.mjs) and the build folder with them; web.yml runs it after the build it already makes. Every ceiling is the value measured on master on 2026-11-12 (Flutter 3.47.5, flutter build web --release --no-web-resources-cdn --pwa-strategy=none) rounded up; it only falls. The first-load and settled ceilings were raised on 2026-11-14 (measured 8500193): the application code is one unit until it is split by area (#3828), so every feature adds to the first download; they fall again with that split. To RAISE one: change the number here in the PR that needs it and give the reason in that PR's text; a raise with no reason is a review finding. To LOWER one: do it in the PR that made the build smaller.

first_load_wire_bytes.measures: Bytes on the wire (gzip for text, raw for images) of every request a cold browser makes until Flutter shows its first frame: index, bootstrap, canvaskit engine (2.1 MB), main.dart.js (6.0 MB), fonts, the manifest and the few assets the first screen reads. The first download a visitor waits for.
first_load_wire_bytes.raise: Only when a feature genuinely belongs in the first frame; say in the PR why it cannot load on demand.

settled_wire_bytes.measures: The same trace up to three quiet seconds after the first frame: what the first screen has fetched once the app is idle. Equal to the first-load number today because nothing is fetched after the first frame without a click.
settled_wire_bytes.raise: Only when something is prefetched on purpose; say what and why in the PR.

on_demand_asset_bytes.measures: Raw size of build/web/assets/assets: the declared pubspec assets (help images, help texts, the instance bundle, demo data) that are fetched only when a screen reads them. Not part of the first download; this keeps them from growing unseen.
on_demand_asset_bytes.raise: A new guide image or help text raises it by its own size; state the size and the guide in the PR.

deployment_bytes.measures: Raw size of every file in build/web, the whole deployment the static host stores and serves.
deployment_bytes.raise: Only with the reason in the PR text; a larger deployment with a flat first load needs a one-line explanation of what was added.
